newsitem.title: USA: Alkermes Phase II trial falls short.
newsitem.headline: Alkermes Phase II trial falls short.

text.p: Alkermes Inc said Monday that preliminary results of its third Phase II trial of its drug delivery agent RMP-7 failed to meet the primary endpoint, but the company will progress to Phase III clinical trials.

Alkermes previously did two successful Phase II trials of the agent. If the third had met the endpoint, Alkermes would have gone straight to the Food and Drug Administration for approval, bypassing Phase III trials.
"Now we will proceed, as normal, through Phase III trials," Alkermes Chief Executive Officer Richard Pops said.
The RMP-7 agent was administered intraveneously in conjunction with the chemotherapeutic agent carboplatin in patients with recurrent malignant brain tumors, it said.
The study did not meet its primary endpoint of time to tumor progression, the company said.
The first two Phase II clinical trials, conducted in Europe, employed a different carboplatin dosing regimen than the U.S. trial and had different patient enrollment criteria, it said.

"These data, when completed and analyzed together with data from our two previously completed European Phase II studies, will provide us with information necessary for designing a Phase III clinical trial of RMP-7 and carboplatin in patients with recurrent brain tumors," Pops said.
